title: Third Epistle of John
context: These blocks come from the Third Epistle of John in the Westcott-Hort Greek New Testament: a very short personal Koine Greek letter from the Elder to Gaius, commending hospitality to travelling missionaries and contrasting Diotrephes with Demetrius, in the plain style of the Johannine letters. Some opening words are printed in capitals in this edition; interpret them by meaning. Keep repeated Johannine terms such as ἀλήθεια, ἀγάπη, and μένω consistent across the letter. Do not reproduce the wording of a particular English Bible.
